BiblicalUsage: The word names the depths, the deep waters where a man sinks and cannot stand, and the psalms cry out from them. David says he is come into deep waters where the floods overflow him, and again he cries that the floods would not overflow him nor the deep swallow him up. The psalmist cries out of the depths to the LORD, and Isaiah says God made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the depths are where prayer begins, because a man who cannot stand learns to cry out. I hold that God made the depths themselves a road for His ransomed, so the very waters that would drown us become the way home.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
